paragraphs: Mutual information measures how much two random variables tell us about one another. When their underlying distributions are unavailable, neural estimators try to infer this dependence from samples. Evaluating those estimates requires knowing the correct answer, which has encouraged researchers to use mathematically convenient datasets whose mutual information can be calculated exactly.

This paper develops a benchmark using images and text, bringing evaluation closer to the complexity of unstructured data. Its construction combines positive pairs sampled from the same class with a binary symmetric channel technique. Together, these tools let the researchers manipulate the true mutual information while retaining real-world data as the material being evaluated.

The authors use the benchmark to investigate seven challenging scenarios for neural estimators. The contribution is a way to test reliability where realistic inputs and controlled reference values coexist. This matters because success on analytically convenient distributions alone provides an incomplete picture of how an estimator handles the dependencies found in images and language.
neurips-2024-a-benchmark-suite-for-evalu.tldr: A new benchmark makes mutual information controllable in image and text datasets so neural estimators can be evaluated on realistic inputs.

paragraphs: Calling a language model repeatedly and voting over its answers can improve performance, but the benefit need not grow with every additional call. This paper studies that relationship for two simple systems: Vote, which aggregates answers by majority voting, and Filter-Vote, which also uses language model filters before aggregation.

Across multiple language tasks, the authors observe performance that initially improves and then declines as the number of calls increases. Their theoretical explanation centers on differences in question difficulty. More calls improve performance on queries classified as easy in the analysis, while worsening it on hard queries. A task containing both types can therefore have a performance peak at an intermediate number of calls.

The authors turn this explanation into analytical scaling models that estimate system performance and identify a suitable call count from a small number of samples. Experiments show accurate predictions for the studied systems. The practical implication is that allocating more inference computation requires understanding the aggregation procedure and the task's mixture of difficulties.
neurips-2024-are-more-llm-calls-all-you-.tldr: Repeated language model calls can eventually hurt voting-based systems, and a model of query difficulty helps predict the best call count.

paragraphs: Inverting diffusion sampling means recovering the initial noise corresponding to a generated sample. Existing training-free methods can provide exact inversion, but the abstract identifies weaknesses in their sampling quality and theoretical understanding. This paper develops a shared mathematical framework for studying those methods and designing improved alternatives.

The framework, Bidirectional Explicit Linear Multi-step sampling, or BELM, derives from numerical methods that allow variable step sizes and formulas. It adds a constraint that makes the procedure explicit in both directions, which the authors identify as central to mathematically exact inversion. Previously proposed heuristic exact inversion samplers appear as special cases within this formulation.

The authors analyze local truncation error, the numerical error associated with an individual step, and find that earlier designs are suboptimal by this criterion. They derive O-BELM by minimizing that error and analyze its stability and global convergence. Experiments demonstrate exact inversion alongside high-quality sampling, while image editing and interpolation experiments illustrate possible applications of the improved sampler.
neurips-2024-belm-bidirectional-explicit.tldr: BELM unifies exact-inversion diffusion samplers and derives an optimized sampler with theoretical guarantees and high-quality experimental results.

paragraphs: Matrix completion reconstructs missing entries from the entries that are observed. Matrix factorization provides a useful setting for studying implicit regularization: the tendency of training to favor particular solutions without explicitly requesting them. This paper investigates why training can favor either low nuclear norm or low rank, two distinct measures of matrix simplicity.

The authors empirically identify the connectivity of observed data as an important influence. As additional observations move the data from disconnected to connected, they observe a shift from low nuclear norm toward low rank. To explain the training process, they identify a hierarchy of invariant manifolds, structured regions of the optimization landscape that guide movement from lower-rank toward higher-rank solutions.

Their theoretical account characterizes training as traversal through this hierarchy and includes the disconnected case. They also establish conditions guaranteeing minimum nuclear norm and give a condition on the dynamics for ensuring minimum rank. These conditional results connect the observed data pattern to the solutions training favors, rather than assigning matrix factorization one universal implicit bias.
neurips-2024-connectivity-shapes-implici.tldr: The connectivity of observed entries helps explain when matrix factorization favors low nuclear norm or low rank during matrix completion.

paragraphs: Multi-head attention contributes substantially to language models' inference computation and memory use. Sharing or removing attention heads can reduce these costs, but may damage performance or require extensive continued training. This paper proposes Decoupled-Head Attention, or DHA, using redundancy among attention heads to make that conversion more efficient.

DHA separately configures sharing groups for key heads and value heads across layers. This flexibility lets the arrangement adapt to the model under a specified head budget. The conversion begins with an existing multi-head attention checkpoint and progressively combines the parameters of similar heads through linear fusion, aiming to preserve knowledge already present in the checkpoint.

In the reported experiments, DHA uses 0.25% of the original pretraining budget to retain 96.1% of performance while reducing the KV cache by 75%. Compared with Group-Query Attention, the authors report fivefold training acceleration and performance improvements under small continued-pretraining budgets. These results support adaptive head sharing as a practical way to trade attention memory against model performance.
neurips-2024-dha-learning-decoupled-head.tldr: DHA progressively fuses similar attention heads with separate key and value sharing to reduce inference memory while retaining much of the original model's performance.

paragraphs: Neural image compression depends on an entropy model that helps encode an image's representation efficiently. The model must balance decoding speed with the tradeoff between file size and reconstruction quality. Recent approaches reduce the number of modeling steps and use varied contexts from backward adaptation, but this paper identifies an information bottleneck in their forward adaptation.

Specifically, those approaches retain a single type of hyper latent representation for forward adaptation. The authors argue that this supplies insufficient context, especially at the first modeling step. Their framework introduces two additional context types and a method for using the combined information to contextualize the elements currently being encoded or decoded.

The approach aims to supply richer context without compromising bit rate. Experiments on popular datasets show consistent improvements in rate-distortion performance across several bit-rate regions, including a reported 3.73% BD-rate gain over the state-of-the-art baseline on Kodak. The finding indicates that the diversity and use of contextual information remain valuable design choices for efficient neural codecs.
neurips-2024-diversify-contextualize-and.tldr: Adding and effectively combining more types of context improves neural image compression's rate-distortion performance.

paragraphs: Vertical federated learning lets organizations jointly train a model when each holds different features of shared instances. In practical collaborations, the identifiers used to connect records may be fuzzy rather than exact. Handling both uncertain links and many participating organizations is difficult for methods designed around only one of those challenges.

Federated Transformer, or FeT, addresses this combination by encoding fuzzy identifiers into data representations and distributing a transformer architecture across the parties. This makes information about record linkage part of the model's representation. The authors also develop a privacy framework that combines differential privacy with secure multi-party computation to protect local representations while limiting the resulting loss of utility.

Experiments report accuracy improvements of up to 46% over baseline models when scaling to 50 parties. FeT also improves performance and privacy in the evaluated two-party fuzzy setting. These findings support treating linkage uncertainty, collaboration across many parties, and representation privacy as connected aspects of the learning problem.
neurips-2024-federated-transformer-multi.tldr: FeT combines distributed transformers and privacy mechanisms to improve federated learning across many parties with fuzzily linked records.

paragraphs: Searching for new crystalline materials involves a chemical space too large to explore exhaustively through experiments. FlowLLM approaches this problem with a generative model that combines a language model's ability to propose structured candidates with a separate model that refines their geometry. The two stages operate on different representations of the same candidate material.

First, a fine-tuned language model learns a starting distribution of metastable crystals represented as text. Its samples are then converted into graphs. A Riemannian flow matching model iteratively adjusts atomic coordinates and lattice parameters, giving the initial proposals a dedicated geometric refinement stage.

The authors report more than a threefold increase in the generation rate of stable materials over state-of-the-art methods, alongside an approximately 50% improvement in the rate of crystals that are simultaneously stable, unique, and novel. Compared with another leading model, generated crystals are also closer to their relaxed states, reducing subsequent computational work. The results support combining learned initial proposals with geometric refinement for material generation.
neurips-2024-flowllm-flow-matching-for-m.tldr: FlowLLM refines language-model-generated crystals with Riemannian flow matching, improving stable material generation and reducing subsequent relaxation costs.

paragraphs: Goal-conditioned reinforcement learning trains a policy to pursue different goals. Hindsight Experience Replay helps by reinterpreting encountered states as goals that were achieved. This becomes problematic when rewards depend on several states and actions across time: a single encountered state cannot provide the required hindsight goal, leaving learning with too little useful feedback.

The proposed GCPO framework uses an on-policy approach with two components. It first pretrains the policy on demonstrations to establish an initial ability to achieve goals. During online learning, it estimates the policy's current capabilities from historical evaluations and selects progressively harder goals. This creates a curriculum tied to what the policy can currently accomplish.

The authors evaluate GCPO on fixed-wing UAV velocity vector control, a long-horizon task with multiple goals. Results show that it can address both Markovian rewards and rewards that depend on a longer history. The contribution connects an initial demonstration-based foundation with adaptive goal selection, addressing the curriculum difficulties that arise when hindsight replay accumulates unsuccessful trajectories.
neurips-2024-goal-conditioned-on-policy-.tldr: GCPO combines demonstration pretraining and an adaptive goal curriculum to learn tasks with both immediate-state and history-dependent rewards.

paragraphs: Photo finishing requires choosing settings in an image-processing pipeline to produce a desired appearance. Automating this process is difficult when searching through many parameters takes numerous pipeline evaluations. Another approach trains a differentiable substitute for the pipeline, but constructing that substitute can itself be challenging.

This paper trains a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy that adjusts parameters iteratively while treating the finishing pipeline as a black box. A goal image tells the policy what result to pursue. The framework therefore learns how to choose parameter updates without requiring a differentiable proxy of the underlying image-processing system.

The authors report finding desired parameters within 10 queries using the trained policy, compared with the 200 queries normally required by optimization-based approaches in their comparison. The conditioning can use a pixel-aligned target, a style image, or another visually representable goal. Experiments on photo finishing and stylization demonstrate the method's advantages, supporting a reusable policy as an efficient mechanism for image-guided parameter tuning.
neurips-2024-goal-conditioned-reinforcem.tldr: A goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy tunes black-box photo finishing pipelines using a target image and relatively few pipeline queries.

paragraphs: Neural networks can learn useful internal features, yet some theoretical descriptions place them in a regime where those features do not change. Other analyses have shown how feature learning occurs during the first steps of training. This paper examines a further mechanism in regularized two-layer networks, focusing on what can happen later.

The central result is a local convergence analysis: once the loss falls below a particular threshold, gradient descent with a carefully regularized objective captures ground-truth directions. The threshold and the regularization are essential conditions of the claim. The result describes feature learning within that favorable training region, rather than asserting that any network or training run must recover those directions.

The authors strengthen the analysis by incorporating results about early-stage feature learning. This connects the initial development of useful features with their continued learning toward the end of training. The work expands the theoretical picture of when feature learning can occur and shows that its role need not be confined to the first gradient updates.
neurips-2024-how-does-gradient-descent-l.tldr: A conditional convergence analysis shows that carefully regularized two-layer networks can continue learning ground-truth feature directions late in training.

paragraphs: Recognizing visible content does not fully capture the ability to understand what an image implies. II-Bench evaluates this higher-order aspect of image understanding in multimodal language models. Its purpose is to examine capabilities that can remain underexplored even as models improve on other visual benchmarks.

The authors find a substantial performance gap between the evaluated models and humans. The best model accuracy reaches 74.8%, while humans average 90% and reach a maximum of 98%. Models also perform worse on abstract and complex images, suggesting difficulties with high-level meaning and with capturing the visual details needed to interpret such images.

A further experiment adds hints about image sentiment polarity to the prompts. Most models improve with these hints, which the authors interpret as evidence of weakness in independently understanding image sentiment. Together, the findings identify image implication as a useful evaluation target and show that assistance with emotional meaning can change measured performance. The benchmark provides a shared resource for investigating these capabilities.
neurips-2024-ii-bench-an-image-implicati.tldr: II-Bench finds substantial gaps between multimodal models and humans in understanding image implications, particularly for abstract or complex images.

paragraphs: Removing an object from a reconstructed 3D scene exposes regions that were hidden in the original views. A diffusion model can invent plausible content for one image, but generating each viewpoint independently can produce conflicting geometry or appearance. In-N-Out addresses the challenge of making these invented regions agree across views.

The method first fills the hidden region in a single view, then extends that result to other views by aligning latent representations. The authors identify two main sources of output variation: the initial sampled latents and the intermediate latents produced during denoising. A Neural Radiance Field aligns the initial latents to establish a consistent structure, while cross-view attention aligns intermediate information to improve appearance consistency.

A patch-based hybrid loss further optimizes the Neural Radiance Field for rendering. The reported results show improved fidelity and coherence in the completed 3D representations. The approach matters because it coordinates the generative process across viewpoints, allowing knowledge learned from 2D images to support a more consistent 3D reconstruction after object removal.
neurips-2024-in-n-out-lifting-2d-diffusi.tldr: In-N-Out aligns diffusion latents across viewpoints to fill regions exposed by 3D object removal with more consistent structure and appearance.

paragraphs: Understanding a learned function can require identifying how groups of inputs interact. The Möbius transform assigns importance coefficients to sets of variables, capturing higher-order interactions alongside connections to familiar game-theoretic importance measures. Its difficulty is scale: a function with n inputs has 2^n possible coefficients.

The authors exploit functions whose transforms are sparse and low-degree, meaning relatively few coefficients are nonzero and interactions involve small groups of inputs. Under certain assumptions, their non-adaptive algorithm recovers K nonzero coefficients using O(Kn) samples and O(Kn²) time. Non-adaptive recovery means the queries need not be chosen in response to earlier answers.

A connection to group testing yields O(Kt log n) sample complexity when interactions involve at most t inputs, with O(K poly(n)) computation time. A robust version tolerates noise while retaining these complexity bounds. The algorithms are developed in an idealized setting, but the authors find relevant structure in many real-world functions, supporting the transform's potential as a tool for interpreting learned models.
neurips-2024-learning-to-understand-iden.tldr: Sparse, low-degree structure enables more efficient recovery of Möbius interaction coefficients, including a noise-tolerant method connected to group testing.

paragraphs: Abstract visual reasoning requires discovering rules that organize visual elements across a puzzle. Existing benchmarks cover limited combinations of patterns, shapes, and layouts. MARVEL broadens this evaluation with 770 puzzles built around six core knowledge patterns, geometric and abstract shapes, and five task configurations.

The benchmark also separates questions about visual perception from the main reasoning questions. This hierarchical structure helps investigate whether failure comes from understanding the visible features or inferring the rule connecting them. The authors evaluate ten representative multimodal language models in zero-shot and few-shot settings, finding near-random performance and a reported 40% gap from humans across patterns and configurations.

The perception questions reveal that the models also struggle to understand the visual features themselves. When textual descriptions are added, some closed-source models, including GPT-4V, show reasoning-pattern understanding comparable to humans. This finding suggests that stronger reasoning can be obstructed by weak perception, making the distinction between seeing the relevant information and reasoning over it central to interpreting benchmark results.
neurips-2024-marvel-multidimensional-abs.tldr: MARVEL finds near-random visual puzzle performance in tested multimodal models and identifies weak perception as an obstacle to their reasoning abilities.

paragraphs: Identifying a protein's active sites requires locating the residues involved in its function. Protein language models learn from abundant amino acid sequences, but precise residue-level functional annotations are scarce. This paper uses textual descriptions of proteins as an additional source of context for improving active-site identification.

The authors construct ProTAD, a dataset containing more than 570,000 pairs of protein sequences and descriptions covering multiple attributes. Their MMSite framework brings together protein language models and biomedical language models. It uses manual prompting and a module called MACross to handle the different attributes expressed in the text.

Training follows two stages: soft-label alignment first brings the sequence and text modalities into correspondence, and multimodal fusion then supports active-site prediction. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance compared with existing protein representation learning methods. The contribution shows how descriptive information can complement sequence representations when detailed functional labels are limited, with both the paired dataset and the framework supporting this combined approach.
neurips-2024-mmsite-a-multi-modal-framew.tldr: MMSite aligns and fuses protein sequences with descriptive text to improve active-site identification.

paragraphs: Pipeline parallelism distributes model training across stages, making the schedule of work important for both memory and throughput. This paper introduces a systematic way to describe schedules as repeated building blocks. The authors show that a building block's lifespan determines the schedule's peak activation memory.

Using this connection, they design a family of building blocks with controllable memory requirements. The proposed schedules can halve peak activation memory relative to 1F1B without sacrificing efficiency, or reduce it to one-third with comparable throughput. Another operating point achieves almost no pipeline bubbles, the idle gaps in pipeline execution, while matching 1F1B's activation memory.

Evaluations report throughput gains of 7% to 55% over 1F1B in pure pipeline parallelism settings. With a grid search over hybrid parallelism choices in practical language model settings, the reported improvement is 16%. These results show how a structural understanding of scheduling can expose useful memory-throughput tradeoffs and guide schedule design beyond choosing among existing patterns.
neurips-2024-pipeline-parallelism-with-c.tldr: A building-block view of pipeline schedules enables controllable activation memory and improves training throughput over 1F1B.

paragraphs: Users can have very different frequency distributions, such as different patterns of word use on their devices. This paper studies how to estimate a personalized distribution for every user in a federated setting while protecting privacy. It measures estimation error with KL divergence and addresses both differences between users and unequal amounts of user data.

The approach discovers groups of users with similar distributions and uses those groups to support personalization. The authors first develop a non-private clustering algorithm, then give a provably jointly differentially private version with private, data-dependent initialization. A model based on mixtures of Dirichlet distributions provides a formal motivation for the non-private algorithm and helps explain properties of its components.

Experiments on Reddit, StackOverflow, and Amazon Reviews vary both statistical heterogeneity and differences in data size. The private and non-private methods improve over standard and clustering-based baselines. In particular, the findings show that discovering similar subpopulations can outperform directly personalizing a single global model in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-private-and-personalized-fr.tldr: Clustering similar users improves personalized frequency estimation, with a jointly differentially private version protecting user information.

paragraphs: The geometric median is the point minimizing the sum of Euclidean distances to a dataset's points. Computing it with differential privacy introduces an accuracy challenge. Standard approaches such as private gradient descent require advance knowledge of a ball containing the data, and their excess error grows linearly with that ball's radius.

This paper asks whether private estimation can instead adapt to the unknown radius containing most of the data. Its main contribution is two polynomial-time algorithms whose excess error guarantees scale with the data's effective diameter. This ties the guarantee to a more representative measure of data spread rather than relying only on the broader enclosing radius.

The authors also propose an inefficient algorithm based on inverse smooth sensitivity that satisfies the stricter requirement of pure differential privacy. A lower bound establishes sample-complexity optimality for the polynomial-time algorithms. Together, these results address accuracy, computational efficiency, and privacy strength, with distinct contributions for efficient estimation and the stronger pure-privacy requirement.
neurips-2024-private-geometric-median-d3.tldr: New private geometric median algorithms achieve error guarantees tied to effective data diameter and optimal sample complexity.

paragraphs: Researchers sometimes compare language models' survey answers with human populations to infer which demographics, opinions, or values the models represent. This paper tests the reliability of that interpretation using the American Community Survey. The authors evaluate 43 language models with prompting methods commonly used for this kind of analysis.

They find that answer order and labels strongly influence responses, including a preference for options labeled A. When the researchers randomize answer ordering to adjust for those biases, the models' responses trend toward a uniform distribution across options. This pattern appears across the evaluated models regardless of their size or training data.

That behavior can create misleading apparent similarities to human groups. A group whose aggregate survey statistics happen to be closer to uniform will appear better represented by the model. The findings therefore challenge interpreting survey-response similarity as straightforward evidence of model alignment: in this evaluation, response-format biases and near-uniform answering patterns can shape the apparent demographic match.
neurips-2024-questioning-the-survey-resp.tldr: Survey answers from 43 language models show formatting biases and near-uniform patterns that can mislead conclusions about demographic alignment.

paragraphs: Diffusion-based image restoration models can produce realistic images, yet severe degradation can lead them to invent incorrect content or textures. The paper attributes this difficulty to heavy reliance on the knowledge stored in model weights. ReFIR adds relevant external images to support restoration with more information.

The framework first uses nearest-neighbor lookup to retrieve high-quality images with content related to the degraded input. It then applies cross-image injection, a mechanism that lets an existing restoration model use textures from those references. Retrieval and injection work together: one supplies relevant visual material, while the other makes that material available during restoration.

The reported experiments demonstrate results that combine fidelity with visual realism and show that external knowledge helps address hallucinated details. ReFIR requires no training and can adapt to various large restoration models. Its contribution is a way to extend the information available to an existing model during restoration, supporting more faithful detail generation when the input itself is severely degraded.
neurips-2024-refir-grounding-large-resto.tldr: ReFIR retrieves relevant high-quality images and injects their textures into restoration models to improve fidelity without additional training.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns categories to image pixels, but labeling every pixel is labor-intensive. Scribbles provide a lighter form of supervision by marking only parts of the image. Although this approach has produced promising models, a shortage of challenging scribble-labeled datasets makes it harder to develop methods and compare them convincingly.

Scribbles for All supplies an algorithm that automatically generates scribble labels from existing dense annotations. The authors use it to provide scribbles for several popular segmentation datasets. Because the procedure applies to datasets that already have dense labels, it creates a route for broadening scribble-supervision research using existing annotated resources.

The paper also evaluates state-of-the-art segmentation models on the resulting datasets. Models trained with synthetic scribbles perform competitively with models trained using manual scribble labels. This supports the generated annotations as useful research material for benchmarking weak supervision. The released datasets, generation algorithm, and baselines provide a shared basis for studying how segmentation models learn from sparse annotations.
neurips-2024-scribbles-for-all-benchmark.tldr: Scribbles for All converts dense segmentation labels into synthetic scribbles that support competitive training and broader benchmarking.

paragraphs: Pruning compresses a language model by introducing sparsity, aiming to reduce its memory and computational demands. Optimizing pruning across an entire large model is difficult to scale. Local pruning is more manageable, but the abstract identifies its solutions as suboptimal, motivating a way to coordinate pruning decisions across the model.

SparseLLM represents the language model as a chain of modular functions and introduces auxiliary variables to decompose the optimization problem. This turns a large global task into smaller, coordinated subproblems. The coordination is central to the framework's stated aim of combining resource-efficient optimization with global optimality.

The authors report significant performance improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods, especially when sparsity is high. This is the setting where the framework's ability to coordinate the decomposed problem is particularly relevant to the reported results. The contribution is a formulation that makes global pruning more practical for large language models while retaining a model-wide optimization perspective, with source code released to support its use.
neurips-2024-sparsellm-towards-global-pr.tldr: SparseLLM decomposes global language-model pruning into coordinated subproblems, improving performance especially at high sparsity.

paragraphs: Teaching an agent a new behavior often requires designing a reward function that captures what success should look like. That work becomes difficult as the desired behaviors multiply. TADPoLe uses a frozen, pretrained text-conditioned diffusion model to supply dense reward signals for policies guided by natural-language descriptions.

The underlying hypothesis is that large generative models contain useful knowledge about both text alignment and natural-looking behavior. TADPoLe uses that knowledge as supervision without requiring a separately designed ground-truth reward or expert demonstrations for the target behaviors. The reward signals are available zero-shot from the pretrained model, while the policy itself is learned through reinforcement learning.

Experiments in Humanoid and Dog environments demonstrate learning of novel goal-achievement and continuous locomotion behaviors. Human evaluations judge the resulting behaviors qualitatively more natural. The method also performs competitively on Meta-World robotic manipulation tasks without in-domain demonstrations. These findings support pretrained generative models as a source of behavior supervision across the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-text-aware-diffusion-for-po.tldr: TADPoLe turns a frozen text-conditioned diffusion model into a reward source for learning language-specified behaviors without expert demonstrations.

paragraphs: This paper studies how a shallow transformer learns to recognize whether two designated words occur together. The authors analyze gradient flow while simultaneously training three attention matrices and a linear MLP from random initialization. Their coupled dynamical-system framework avoids several simplifications commonly used in related analyses, including attention linearization and a lazy training regime.

The analysis identifies two phases. Initially, the linear MLP quickly aligns with the two target signals and enables correct classification, while softmax attention changes very little. Later, attention and the MLP evolve together to enlarge the classification margin and drive the loss close to its minimum.

A key theoretical property is automatic balancing of gradients, which makes different samples' losses decrease at nearly the same rate and helps establish the near-minimum-loss result. The authors also characterize the trained attention model and conduct experiments supporting the theory. Within the studied task, the findings explain how early learning in one component gives way to coordinated improvement across the transformer.
neurips-2024-training-dynamics-of-transf.tldr: A gradient-flow analysis reveals two learning phases in a shallow transformer, from early MLP alignment to joint attention and MLP refinement.
